opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: John Rodriguez (E049) requested write access to Source Code. The two evidence notes conflict on employment type: HR lists him as full-time Analyst (which would permit write, since full-time employees max out at write and admin requires the Engineer role), while Security lists him as a contractor with basic security training (max read, since contractors only get write with advanced training and never admin). With conflicting employment records, I apply the more restrictive security-based assessment: contractor with basic training → maximum is read. Write exceeds the max, so grant read. Do not grant more than the maximum or the requested level.
